newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PLA to delay HK arrival till dawn on July 1 -paper.
newsitem.headline: PLA to delay HK arrival till dawn on July 1 -paper.

text.p: The People's Liberation Army (PLA) will wait until daylight breaks on July 1 before marching into Hong Kong, a Hong Kong newspaper said on Tuesday.
Hong Kong, a British colony for more than 150 years, reverts to China at midnight on June 30, 1997 and many people had expected the PLA to cross the border the moment the British furled their flag.
The Chinese-language Apple Daily said the main garrison would arrive at around 5:00 a.m. to 6:00 a.m. (2100-2200 GMT June 30).
The troops would be inspected by senior Chinese leaders, in Hong Kong to attend the handover ceremony, and Hong Kong's post-colonial leader Tung Chee-hwa, the mass circulation paper said.
A group of senior PLA officials would arrive earlier to attend the historic transition ceremony along with more than 4,000 dignitaries and guests.
Many Hong Kong people remember with horror the PLA's brutal crackdown on student-led demonstrators around Tiananmen Square in 1989 and view the PLA's arrival with trepidation.
